item.dc:creator: Mathias Beiglb\"ock, Manuel Hasenbichler, Gudmund Pammer

item.title: Uniqueness and full coverage in $k$-neighbor graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the number of infinite clusters in the $2dp$-neighbor graph on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge2$, in which every vertex independently selects $\lfloor 2dp\rfloor$ of its nearest neighbors uniformly at random, and one more with probability $2dp-\lfloor 2dp\rfloor$. The model has negatively correlated edges and, for $1\le2dp\le2d-1$, neither finite energy nor insertion or deletion tolerance. We prove that the undirected graph has at most one infinite cluster for every $p\in [0,1]$, and that in the planar case the same holds for forward and strong forward clusters of the directed graph when $p\in[1/2,1]$. We further exhibit a second phase transition: for $p\ge(d+1)/(2d)$ the open cluster of the origin is almost surely the whole lattice, and for $p>(d+1)/(2d)$ any two vertices of a box are connected inside the box of twice the size with probability exponentially close to one. In particular, the percolation function is continuous but not analytic on the supercritical interval $(p_c,1]$. Finally, we prove that the full-coverage phase transition at $p_f = (d+1)/2d$ is of order $2^d$.
item.dc:creator: David Coupier, Beno\^it Henry, Benedikt Jahnel, Jonas K\"oppl

item.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
item.description: arXiv:2611.06845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How well can two independent random samples from a metric measure space be matched while preserving pairwise distances? Concretely, given two independent copies, each of $n$ points sampled from the space, what is their typical metric distortion as finite $n$-point metric spaces? We prove that the space $[0,1]$ equipped with the uniform measure already exhibits a rich behavior. We show that with high probability the distortion of the two independent samples is $n^{2/3}$ up to polylogarithmic factors. The lower bound reflects two competing obstructions. A bijection that maps points close to their original positions or their reflections in $[0,1]$ must expand the smallest gaps, in both directions. On the other hand, we show that large displacement from both the identity and reflection itself forces large distortion. Balancing these obstructions yields the lower-bound exponent $2/3$. For the upper bound, we construct a partial matching of the points that maps each gap between consecutive points of length $d\lesssim n^{-4/3}$ to a pair at distance $\widetilde{O}(dn^{1/3})$, with analogous control in the reverse direction. We then use a delicate multiscale oscillation construction to extend this partial matching to a low-distortion bijection.
item.dc:creator: Itai Benjamini, Mark Braverman, Elad Tzalik, Georgii Zakharov

item.title: Uniform Central Limit Theorems for Degree Distributions of Sparse Graphon Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.06892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The degree distribution is among the most basic summaries of a network, yet no functional limit theorem for the empirical degree distribution of graphon models has been available, even for dense, bounded graphons, for which only finite-dimensional results were known. We study the empirical degree distribution of sparse $L^p$ graphon models, allowing unbounded kernels and hence heavy-tailed degrees. For graphons whose latent expected degrees have a density, we prove a finite-dimensional central limit theorem whenever $n\rho_n/\log n\to\infty$ and $n\rho_n^{2+\beta}\to0$, where $\rho_n$ is the sparsity level and the kernel has $2+\beta$ moments for some $\beta>0$; the limiting covariance coincides with that of the dense case. Under additional local regularity, we establish a functional central limit theorem on compact intervals in the interior of the support. Under tail regularity and a stronger sparsity condition, we prove that uniformity extends to unbounded intervals. We also show that uniform limits fail at atoms of the degree distribution, for instance in stochastic block models. The analysis rests on an exact multilinear representation of the conditional degree distribution, which identifies its Hoeffding decomposition without Edgeworth expansions, combined with a lattice version of Billingsley's tightness criterion and moment inequalities of Efron-Stein type.
item.dc:creator: Robert Lunde, Soumendra Lahiri

item.title: Sublinear multi-type preferential attachment
item.description: arXiv:2611.06904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a random growing graph model with two \emph{types}, or \emph{communities}, that belongs to the class of preferential attachment models. Starting from an initial graph $G_0$ in which each node has a type, the graph $G_{n+1}$ is generated by addition of a new node, which attaches through an edge to a node $v$ of $G_n$. The probability of attaching to $v$ depends on the communities of both the new node and $v$, and is proportional to $\operatorname{deg}_n(v)^\gamma$, where $\gamma\in[0, 1]$. We establish a convergence result for the limiting proportion of vertices of each degree and in each community in a certain regime of the parameter $\gamma$. To this end, we first use stochastic approximation techniques to reduce the convergence problem to the study of a non-linear evolution equation. We then use a probabilistic coupling approach to investigate the long-time behavior of the unique solution to this evolution equation. We emphasize that the techniques previously used to handle the single-community case cannot be extended directly to our setting. Indeed, the associated continuous-time embedding is not a multitype branching process in the usual sense, since the transition rates at any given time $t$ depend on the entire graph structure at that time.
item.dc:creator: Anna Ben-Hamou, Nicolas Broutin, Camille Cazaux

item.title: The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.39242v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.
item.dc:creator: Kuijun Liu, Feng Luo, Yanwen Luo, Zhenghao Rao

item.title: Soft-confinement approximation of no-flux McKean-Vlasov dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.05431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the approximation of the no-flux McKean-Vlasov equation on a bounded convex domain by a whole-space equation with quadratic confinement of strength $\lambda^{-1}$ outside the domain. For a smooth bounded interaction kernel and a common bounded initial density with square-integrable gradient, we establish an $O(\lambda^{1/4})$ approximation rate. The estimate controls the $L^2$ density error uniformly on every finite time interval and the gradient error in space-time $L^2$. Without interaction, a spectral gap independent of $\lambda$ yields the $O(\lambda^{1/4})$ rate uniformly in time for the density error and uniformly over all unit time intervals for the gradient error. With interaction, we construct a counterexample showing that even weak convergence can fail to be uniform in time.
item.dc:creator: Geuntaek Seo, Yeoneung Kim, Beomjun Choi

item.title: A Fully Polynomial Approximation Algorithm for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.05446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Montanari's incremental approximate message passing (IAMP) algorithm [FOCS 2019; SIAM J. Comput., 2025] and the zero-temperature formulation of El Alaoui, Montanari and Sellke (AMS) [Ann. Probab., 2021] find a $(1-\varepsilon)$ approximation to the maximum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) energy in $C(\varepsilon)N^2$ operations for fixed accuracy, with probability tending to one as $N\to\infty$, under their respective full-support and access-model assumptions. However, it was unknown whether this approximation could be achieved with work polynomial in both $N$ and $1/\varepsilon$, together with quantitative guarantees at finite dimension. Under the same assumptions as AMS, we introduce grouped IAMP with exact Gaussian query outputs (GEG-IAMP), which is the first SK approximation algorithm with total work polynomial in $N$ and $1/\varepsilon$ and a finite-size guarantee above a dimension threshold polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$ and $\log(1/\alpha)$. More precisely, for every $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$, it returns a $(1-\varepsilon)$ approximation with probability at least $1-\alpha$ whenever $N\ge \mathsf{K}\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(e/\varepsilon)\log(\mathsf{K}/\alpha)$, using $O(N^2/\varepsilon)$ work and $O(N^2)$ storage. GEG-IAMP replaces the Onsager correction by Reeves's coupling construction [arXiv:2508.10782] and groups Euler-Maruyama steps into $O(1/\varepsilon)$ matrix-vector products. We also prove a relative guarantee for AMS IAMP with $O(N^2\varepsilon^{-3}\log^2(e/\varepsilon))$ work but a sufficient dimension exponential in inverse accuracy. By returning a fixed configuration below its dimension threshold, GEG-IAMP also provides an asymptotic fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme (AFPRAS), with an additive error independent of dimension.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Herman, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul

item.title: Low moments of sums of extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X^e \colon \mathbb{N} \to \{\pm 1\}$ be the random, completely multiplicative function whose values at the primes $(X^e(p))_{p \text{ prime}}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\{ \pm 1 \}$. Let $X=X^e\mu^2$. We determine the order of magnitude of \[ \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg| \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\sum_{n \le x} X^e(n) \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]\quad \text{ and }\quad \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg|\sum_{n \le x} \frac{X(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg] \] for $q\in [0,1]$, showing that a transition from better-than-square-root cancellation to growth like a power of $\log x$ occurs when $q$ crosses $1/2$. In particular, the first absolute moments are of order $(\log\log x)^{3/4}$. The proof proceeds by comparing these sums to integrals of random Euler products, which are then studied by analogy with Gaussian multiplicative chaos integrals. The main difficulty lies in proving the lower bound at $q=1/2$, for which we also adapt arguments from the study of random walks.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Atherfold, Maxim Gerspach, Jad Hamdan

item.title: Rough-to-frozen transition in non-integrable dimer models
item.description: arXiv:2611.05516v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The transition from rough to frozen phases in models of random surfaces is expected to be governed by the Pokrovsky-Talapov law, which predicts a $\varepsilon^{3/2}$-type singularity of the macroscopic height profile (limit shape), as the distance $\varepsilon$ from the frozen phase (facet) is sent to zero. This has been proved so far only in exactly solvable cases, notably the classical, determinantal, 2D dimer model. In this paper we prove the validity of the Pokrovsky-Talapov law for a non-integrable 2D dimer model on the hexagonal lattice, whose Gibbs weight depends upon a weak plaquette interaction among dimers. Our proof is based on a multiscale analysis (constructive fermionic Renormalization Group), which allows us to identify two different regimes with distinct scaling properties and to explain the universality of the Pokrovsky-Talapov exponent $3/2$, in contrast with the interaction-dependent critical exponents characterizing the rough phase. The first regime, corresponding to smaller distances, is characterized by an effective quadratic dispersion relation, while the second comes with an effective linear dispersion relation, typical of Luttinger liquid behavior. As a byproduct of our construction, we control the scaling limit of the interacting dimer model uniformly in the distance from the frozen phase.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Giuliani, Vieri Mastropietro, Bruno Renzi, Fabio Toninelli

item.title: One-third H\"older stability of optimal transport maps from log-concave sources
item.description:
arXiv:2611.05534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove quantitative stability of quadratic optimal transport maps from arbitrary log-concave sources to bounded targets. If the source $ho$ is isotropic on $\mathbb R^d$ and the targets $\mu$, $
u$ are supported in a common ball of radius $R$, their Brenier maps satisfy \[ \lVert T_\mu-T_
uVert_{L^2(ho)} \leqslant 17d^{2/3}R^{2/3}W_2(\mu,
u)^{1/3}. \] The one-third exponent is optimal for $d\geqslant2$. The proof combines a linear stability estimate for Brenier potentials in a weighted norm with a matching weighted reverse Poincar'e inequality. The weight is chosen in terms of the negative log-density of the source to account for its tails. We also show that the best dimensional constant in map stability is at least of order $d^{1/3}$.
item.dc:creator: Songbo Wang, Xiaozhen Wang

item.title: Linear-length cycles in the supercritical percolated hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2611.05634v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $Q_p^d$ be the random subgraph of the $d$-dimensional binary hypercube obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. A long-standing folklore conjecture states that the emergence of the giant component in $Q_p^d$, at $p\approx 1/d$, is accompanied by the emergence of cycles of linear length. We confirm this conjecture and determine the order of the longest cycle near the phase transition. Specifically, for every sufficiently small constant $\varepsilon>0$, we show that if $p=(1+\varepsilon)/d$, then with high probability the longest cycle of $Q_p^d$ has length $\Theta(\varepsilon^2 2^d)$. The dependence on $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to constant factors.
item.dc:creator: Michael Anastos

item.title: A liquid vapor phase transition in quantum statistical mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2611.05641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a liquid vapor phase transition for a quantum system of particles in the continuum. The system is the quantum version with Boltzmann statistics of the point particles model introduced in by Lebowitz, Mazel and Presutti.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Baffioni, Tobias Kuna, Immacolata Merola, Errico Presutti

item.title: Functional inequalities from the fundamental limits of Bayesian estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.05831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a Bayesian information-theoretic framework for proving functional inequalities for log-concave measures. Motivated by Klartag and Ordentlich, we establish a unified equivalence between $\Phi$-Sobolev inequalities and Bayesian estimation lower bounds: for a large class of smooth convex $\Phi$, a log-concave measure $\mu$ satisfies a $\Phi$-Sobolev inequality with constant $C>0$ if and only if for $X\sim\mu$, any $t>0$, and any real-valued measurable $f$, the Bayes risk of estimating $f(X)$ under the $\Phi$-Bregman loss from the Gaussian additive observation $Y_t=\sqrt tX+G, G\sim N(0,I_n)$ is at least a $1/(1+Ct)$-fraction of that of the trivial estimator. Combining it with direct information-theoretic arguments, such as testing-to-estimation reductions, we obtain old and new functional inequalities: - For the Poincar\'e inequality, corresponding to $\Phi(x)=(x-1)^2$, we give a simple static information-theoretic proof that the Poincar\'e constant of an isotropic log-concave measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $O(n^{1/2})$, first proven via stochastic localization in the seminal work of Lee and Vempala. - For the log-Sobolev inequality, corresponding to $\Phi(x)=x\log x$, we prove that all smooth $K$-subgaussian log-concave measures $\mu$ satisfy $C_{\mathrm{LS}}(\mu)\lesssim K^2n^{1/4}$, surpassing the recent state-of-the-art bound of $O(K^2n^{1/2})$ by Bizeul. In parallel and independent work, OpenAI claimed the optimal bound $O(K^2)$ in their October 6, 2026 release of 722 papers. - Finally, we give a Bayesian reformulation of the common structure of the three recent proofs of the Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits conjecture, a dimension-free Poincar\'e bound for isotropic log-concave measures [BK26; BKL26; SZ26]. Tools from the study of the "low-degree MMSE" in computational complexity of statistical inference motivate and recast key steps and quantities of these proofs.
item.dc:creator: Shuchen Li, Ilias Zadik

item.title: Empirical approximation of $L^p$ norms for $p\in (1, 2)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.05930v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $p\in[1,2]$, we prove uniform moment estimates for weighted sums \[ \sum_{j=1}^m\zeta_jw_j|\langle{\bf v}_j,y\rangle|^p \] of independent subgaussian random variables $\zeta_j$, where the unit vectors $\{{\bf v}_j\}_{j=1}^m$ and nonnegative weights $\{w_j\}_{j=1}^m$ form an isotropic frame. This allows us to obtain optimal sampling discretization of $L_p$ norms for each fixed $p\in[1,2]$. Namely, for an $N$-dimensional space $X_N$ of bounded functions satisfying $\|f\|_\infty\le\sqrt {KN}\,\|f\|_{L_2}$ for every $f\in X_N$, we show that $m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}KN\log(2N)$ independent samples $\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^m$ provide the discretization \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(\xi^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \quad\forall f\in X_N \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This implies a corresponding weighted discretization result that, for $1<p<2$, improves Talagrand's bound on the dimension $m$ needed to embed $N$-dimensional subspaces of $L_p$ into $\ell_p^m$ with distortion at most $1+\varepsilon$, giving $m\le C\varepsilon^{-2}N\log(2N)$.
item.dc:creator: Feng Dai, Egor Kosov

item.title: Can a self-sustaining chemical network emerge due to just a few catalysts?
item.description: arXiv:2611.06033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding how self-sustaining chemical reaction networks can emerge from simple molecules is an important question in chemical approaches to the origin of life. Reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated (RAF) sets provide a mathematical framework for investigating this question. This line of research goes back to the early work of Kauffman on autocatalytic reaction networks and was subsequently developed through the probabilistic framework of Mossel and Steel. Further contributions by Hordijk, Steel, and collaborators extended the theory to more heterogeneous forms of catalysis, including reaction-dependent probabilities or power-law distributions of catalytic activity. We introduce a stochastic model that combines heterogeneous molecular catalytic activity with reaction-dependent molecule-reaction compatibility. By assigning random catalytic weights to molecules and incorporating compatibility through an explicit formulation of catalysis probabilities, our model provides a concrete and flexible setting that captures both sources of heterogeneity while remaining mathematically tractable. We establish novel and general criteria for RAF formation and nonformation. We further demonstrate that classical phase-transition criteria need not remain valid in the presence of reaction-dependent catalysis. For heavy-tailed catalytic weights, we identify and rigorously quantify an additional phase transition. In models with finite-mean catalytic weights, RAF formation and nonformation are governed by a catalytic intensity parameter. For infinite-mean weights, however, we show that RAFs may emerge with probability tending to one even when the catalytic intensity parameter tends to zero.
item.dc:creator: Jinsu Kim, Ercan S\"onmez

item.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
item.description: arXiv:2611.06041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $\rho_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/\rho_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_\beta N^{-\beta}$ for every $0<\beta<1$, with $c_\beta>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.
item.dc:creator: Bo Tan, Zhen Zhang, Qing-Long Zhou

item.title: Hadamard configurations and sharp cubic-period bounds for stealth in dimensions 10, 11, and 12
item.description: arXiv:2611.06148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct explicit, nonlattice periodic point configurations in dimensions $10$, $11$ and $12$ with stealth center density $1/24$ and unit-density stealth radius $2\cdot24^{-1/n}$. These values exceed those of duals of the current record lattice packings, without claiming to exceed all possible lattices. The construction uses the $24$ sign rows of an order-$12$ Hadamard matrix and their antipodes, projected onto $n$ coordinates. For an arbitrary, not necessarily binary, equally weighted motif with marked period $2\mathbb{Z}^n$, we prove a sharp $2n$-point lower bound for a raw stealth radius at least one and classify equality by antipodal Hadamard configurations. We deduce bounded-complexity optimality, sharp optimality among binary motifs in dimensions $10$--$12$, and local maximality under simultaneous perturbations of the motif and the marked period shape. A divisibility argument excludes ordinary equally weighted periodic formal duals. Statements are confined to their indicated classes; no global optimality among arbitrary-period configurations is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Josiah Park

item.title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
item.description: arXiv:2611.06151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) can reconstruct fine-scale Earth-observation fields from coarse observations, but reconstruction accuracy alone does not provide a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions. Conformal Mask Calibration (CMC), built on conformal risk control, converts a spatial uncertainty score into a trust mask and controls the expected worst-case local distortion under exchangeability. However, its fixed threshold can become miscalibrated in Earth-observation streams affected by seasonality and episodic events. We propose $\textit{CARM}$ (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking), a statistical framework for adaptive spatial risk control under temporal distribution shift. CARM maintains experts with heterogeneous update rates and aggregates their threshold proposals online using an asymmetric surrogate loss, balancing rapid adaptation to distribution changes against stability during relatively stationary periods. All updates are causal and use only mature feedback available after a fixed delay, allowing CARM to operate with any SR model that provides a spatial uncertainty score. We prove that the time-averaged mask-conditioned risk converges to at most $\alpha$ at an $O(1/T)$ rate, without distributional assumptions and for any choice of aggregation weights across experts. On a daily South China Sea chlorophyll-$\textit{a}$ SR stream, CARM reduces the empirical violation rate from $43.49\%$ to $9.38\%$ and the moving-average exceedance frequency from $47.29\%$ to $1.22\%$ at $\alpha=0.10$, while retaining a non-trivial trusted region. Experiments on ERA5 wind and OSTIA sea-surface temperature further show consistent relative improvements across multiple SR backbones.
item.dc:creator: Guangtao Zhang, Haonan Wu, Junxuan Gao, Zhengyang Liu, Zhaoxi Zeng, Zhihao Li, Jianguo Huang, Zhiqiang Liu

item.title: Variational Splines and Generalized Gaussian Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.06233v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tikhonov regularization, kriging, and Gaussian-process regression share the same algorithm because, for a linear inverse problem with a Gaussian prior and Gaussian noise, the minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) estimator is the solution of a regularized least-squares problem. We show that this equivalence survives the passage from vectors to generalized functions: the regularized least-squares estimators become generalized splines, and the Gaussian random vectors become generalized Gaussian processes (GGPs) on the dual of a nuclear space. A whitening operator $\mathrm{L}: \mathcal{S} \to L_2$ specifies both the native Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L} \subset \mathcal{S}'$ of the splines and a family of GGPs, which solve a stochastic differential equation subject to boundary conditions. We prove that the Gaussian spaces of these processes are congruent to the core $\mathrm{L}^\ast(L_2)$ of the native space, and that their MMSE estimators from finitely many linear measurements are generalized splines. Our framework extends the classical correspondences of Kimeldorf-Wahba, Parzen and Kailath in two respects: our estimators form a broader class that includes generalized functions, and we give a proper Bayesian treatment of the case where the null space of $\mathrm{L}$ is non-trivial. The framework gives a precise meaning to statements such as ``fractional splines are the optimal estimators of fractional Brownian motion,'' and it provides a rigorous Bayesian formulation of infinite-dimensional linear inverse problems.
item.dc:creator: Michael Unser

item.title: An Exact Poisson Mixture Representation of Siler Remaining Life Expectancy
item.description: arXiv:2611.06376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. No standard closed form is available for its remaining life expectancy, which must therefore be evaluated by numerical integration. We show that Siler remaining life expectancy at age $x$ is a Poisson mixture of Gompertz-Makeham remaining life expectancies, that is, a Poisson-weighted average of life expectancies in models with only a constant background hazard and an exponentially increasing senescence hazard. All components share the senescence hazard. Their background hazards increase from one component to the next by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines. The Poisson mean is the immaturity hazard that remains to be accumulated after age $x$. This representation yields an exact series of generalized exponential integrals with a closed-form bound on the truncation error. Replacing the background hazard by its discounted counterpart also gives the Laplace transform of the remaining lifetime. The mixture bounds the life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality: up to a term below the reciprocal of $a_2+b_1$, this loss equals the probability of an immaturity death times the life expectancy with the immaturity hazard removed. In annual Siler fits to Swedish female mortality, we estimate that the loss at birth fell from 4.3 years in 1900 to less than 0.01 years in 2020, which accounts for 15% of the gain in life expectancy at birth over the period.
item.dc:creator: Silvio C. Patricio

item.title: An equivalence principle for martingales
item.description: arXiv:2611.06426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that any discrete-time filtration can be embedded into a dyadic filtration, realized via a non-classical measure-preserving map. This embedding makes it possible to reduce certain problems involving vector-valued martingales to the case of Haar martingales. Some applications of this result will also be discussed.
item.dc:creator: Grigori A. Karagulyan, Linda A. Khachatryan, Khazhakanush V. Navoyan

item.title: A general technique for explicit quantile representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.06459v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work proves existence of contours independent of probability level for exact quantile integrals of strictly positive real-analytic densities. Explicit constructions cover five broad distribution families and yield a finite-interval representation of Black-Scholes implied volatility using forward functions.
item.dc:creator: Wolfgang Schadner

item.title: On Natural Exponential Families with Log-Affine Generalized Variance
item.description: arXiv:2611.06885v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study natural exponential families whose generalized variance, the determinant of the covariance matrix, is log-affine in the natural parameter. Without any assumption on the natural parameter domain, we show that every such family is regular and that it is Gaussian when its generalized variance is constant. Consequently, a sample of size $n>d$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ comes from a non-degenerate normal law exactly when the conditional expectation of the sample generalized variance given the sample mean is a positive constant. Every non-Gaussian family puts mass on a facet of its convex support, and, as for a Poisson count, its height above that facet takes only integer multiples of a fixed step. More generally, its displacement away from any exposed face that carries mass has nonnegative integer coordinates in a suitable basis. A local inequality between third and fourth cumulants singles out the Poisson--Gaussian families and yields a complete classification of the infinitely divisible ones. Geometrically, a semi-flat K\"ahler tube, whose potential has constant Hessian determinant, is flat if some multiple of its metric is projectively induced near a point.
item.dc:creator: Zeyu Cao, Shaosai Huang

item.title: On the minimum bisection of random $3$-regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2009.00598v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we give new bounds on the bisection width of random 3-regular graphs on $n$ vertices. The main contribution is a new lower bound of $0.103295n$ based on a first moment method together with a structural analysis of the graph, thereby improving a 27-year-old result of Kostochka and Melnikov. We also give a complementary upper bound of $0.139822n$ by combining a result of Lyons with original combinatorial insights. Developping this approach further, we obtain a non-rigorous improved upper bound with the help of Monte Carlo simulations.
item.dc:creator: Lyuben Lichev, Dieter Mitsche

item.title: Loewner evolution driven by complex Brownian motion (with simulations by Minjae Park)
item.description: arXiv:2203.07313v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Loewner evolution whose driving function is $W_t = B_t^1 + i B_t^2$, where $(B^1,B^2)$ is a pair of Brownian motions with a given covariance matrix. This model can be thought of as a generalization of Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) with complex parameter values. We show that our Loewner evolutions behave very differently from ordinary SLE. For example, if neither $B^1$ nor $B^2$ is identically equal to zero, then the set of points disconnected from $\infty$ by the Loewner hull has non-empty interior at each time. We also show that our model exhibits three phases analogous to the phases of SLE: a phase where the hulls have zero Lebesgue measure, a phase where points are swallowed but not hit by the hulls, and a phase where the hulls are space-filling. The phase boundaries are expressed in terms of the signs of explicit integrals. These boundaries have a simple closed form when the correlation of the two Brownian motions is zero.
item.dc:creator: Ewain Gwynne, Joshua Pfeffer

item.title: Semimartingale characteristics of the two-dimensional stochastic heat equation at criticality
item.description: arXiv:2504.21791v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize the sample-path structure of the two-dimensional stochastic heat equation at criticality. The main theorems provide a complete, pathwise description of its semimartingale characteristics and establish explicit, exact formulas for the covariation measure. The proof derives an asymptotic expansion for the covariation measures of regularized approximate solutions by integrating techniques from quantum-solvable operators into stochastic integration theory.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Ting Chen

item.title: Asymptotic exponential moments of two-dimensional additive functionals above subcriticality
item.description: arXiv:2504.21796v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce new asymptotic formulas for the exponential moments of rescaled additive functionals of two-dimensional Brownian motion, extending the analysis to parameter regimes that go beyond the subcritical case underlying distributional limits. As an application, we develop a probabilistic-analytic approximation for the two-dimensional Laplacian with a singular perturbation at the origin. This method describes the perturbed Laplacian by combining analytic characteristics of the Kallianpur-Robbins and Kasahara-Kotani laws.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Ting Chen

item.title: Infinite-Time Mean Field FBSDEs and the Associated Elliptic Master Equations
item.description: arXiv:2510.03707v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study discounted infinite-time mean field forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) and the associated elliptic master equations, which were introduced in [20] as mathematical tools for solving discounted infinite-time mean field games. We first establish stability and flow properties, identify the backward decoupling field with the spatial derivative of the equilibrium value function, and prove that the value function is a viscosity solution of the master equation. Under additional smoothness and quantitative stability assumptions, we construct its Lions-derivative and the required higher-order derivatives using variational results from a companion paper [21]. These results show that the value function is a classical solution of the elliptic master equation. We also prove that the value function is the unique displacement-monotone regular solution.
item.dc:creator: Yongsheng Song, Zeyu Yang

item.title: Landau Hamiltonian with Gaussian white noise potential and the asymptotics of the bottom of its spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2511.22162v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a simple construction of a random Schr\"odinger operator subject to a magnetic field with a regularity as low as $0^-$-H\"older and a Gaussian white noise electric potential on a two-dimensional bounded box. This construction is based on the exponential Ansatz introduced in [HL15] and leverages the semigroup approach developed in [HL24]. The proposed construction enables us to generalise an asymptotic result for the bottom of the spectrum of the two-dimensional continuous Anderson Hamiltonian, first proved in [CvZ21], to the magnetic case. Our choice of potential not only covers the case of a uniform magnetic field, but also those which would break translational invariance.
item.dc:creator: Yueh-Sheng Hsu

item.title: Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund-type SLLN for mixed moving average processes
item.description: arXiv:2601.14748v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund theorem is a fundamental result in probability theory that establishes rates of convergence in the strong law of large numbers (SLLN). Although numerous extensions have been developed for dependent sequences, many classes of processes, particularly those exhibiting strong dependence, remain unexplored. In this paper, we present a Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund-type SLLN for a class of mixed moving average processes, which form a large and flexible class of stationary infinitely divisible processes. In contrast to the classical case, where moments determine the asymptotic behavior, the present setting additionally involves key objects that characterize both dependence and marginal distributions.
item.dc:creator: Danijel Grahovac, P\'eter Kevei, Dominik Mihal\v{c}i\'c

item.title: Stochastic analysis for the Dirichlet--Ferguson process
item.description: arXiv:2603.07104v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a Dirichlet--Ferguson process $\zeta$ on a general phase space. First we reprove the chaos expansion from Peccati (2008), providing an explicit formula for the kernel functions. Then we proceed with developing a Malliavin calculus for $\zeta$. To this end we introduce a gradient, a divergence and a generator which act as linear operators on random variables or random fields and which are linked by some basic formulas such as integration by parts. While this calculus is strongly motivated by Malliavin calculus for isonormal Gaussian processes and the general Poisson process, the strong dependence properties of $\zeta$ require considerably more combinatorial efforts. We apply our theory to identify our generator as the generator of the Fleming--Viot process and to describe the associated Dirichlet form explicitly in terms of the chaos expansion. We also establish the product and chain chain rule for the gradient and an integral representation of the divergence. Finally we give a short direct proof of the Poincar\'e inequality and establish a sharp reverse Poincar\'e inequality, similarly to the one in Schulte and Trapp (2024) for the Poisson process.
item.dc:creator: G\"unter Last, Babette Picker

item.title: Clustering without geometry in sparse networks with independent edges
item.description: arXiv:2603.13159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The coexistence of sparsity and clustering (non-vanishing average fraction of triangles per node) is one of the few structural features that, irrespective of finer details, are ubiquitously observed across large real-world networks. This fact calls for generic models producing sparse clustered graphs. Earlier results suggested that sparse random graphs with independent edges fail to reproduce clustering, unless edge probabilities are assumed to depend on underlying metric distances that, thanks to the triangle inequality, naturally favour triadic closure. This observation has opened a debate on whether clustering implies (latent) geometry in real-world networks. Alternatively, recent models of higher-order networks can replicate clustering by abandoning edge independence. In this paper, we mathematically prove, and numerically confirm, that a sparse random graph with independent edges, recently identified in the context of network renormalization as an invariant model under node aggregation, produces finite clustering without any geometric or higher-order constraint. The underlying mechanism is an infinite-mean node fitness, which also implies a power-law degree distribution. Further, as a novel phenomenon that we characterize rigorously, we observe the breakdown of self-averaging of various network properties. Therefore, as an alternative to geometry or higher-order dependencies, node aggregation invariance emerges as a basic route to realistic network properties.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Catanzaro, Remco van der Hofstad, Diego Garlaschelli

item.title: A Distributional Equation Approach to Front Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2604.16956v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Travelling waves of mean-field particle systems are usually studied through the partial differential equation satisfied by the mean-field limit. We develop a different and entirely probabilistic set of tools. The wave profile is characterised as the solution of a distributional fixed-point equation for a tagged particle seen in the frame of the wave, and that equation is solved by relating it to a linear one --- a smoothing transform --- whose solutions are the martingale limits of a branching random walk. We apply this approach to a range of models, recover some known results and obtain a number of new ones. We first study models where particles evolve according to independent L\'evy processes and, at Poisson epochs synchronise randomly selected pairs of particles (the lower of the two moves instantaneously to the position of the higher of the two). We characterise the speeds and travelling waves for all such models. In particular, this covers the case where the L\'evy process is a continuous-time random walk with an arbitrary jump distribution; previously, only exponentially distributed jumps had been treated. We also consider a variant in which, instead of synchronising, the lower of the two particles jumps up by a random amount, drawn independently at each jump. This model is motivated by the so-called power-of-2 systems from queueing theory. Finally, we consider a new model where updates are given by the mixture of synchronisation and power-of-2: each update is a random value but the resulting position of the lower particle is capped by that of the higher one. In all cases, we characterise the speed, the travelling waves and their tail behaviour; the probabilistic nature of our approach makes the tail analysis particularly tractable.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Jonckheere, Seva Shneer

item.title: Interference Queueing Networks: A Replica Mean-Field Approach in the Symmetric Setting
item.description: arXiv:2606.13264v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a model for evaluating the performance of wireless communication networks beyond the ubiquitous full-buffer assumption, under which every transmitter is always active. The network is represented by N interacting queues arranged on a torus, with homogeneous arrival rate and service rates depending on the activity of neighboring interferers. More precisely, each queue is associated with a transmitter-receiver pair, and its service rate is given by the Shannon capacity, which depends on the corresponding Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR). Since interfering transmitters only emit when their queue is non-empty, the SINR, and hence the service rate, improves when neighboring queues are empty. We first derive the stability region of the system. To investigate the stationary regime, we introduce two mean-field approximations. The first one is obtained from a finite K-replica system, for which we prove propagation of chaos as K goes to infinity. The second one describes a queueing system evolving in a suitably chosen environment. We derive quantitative estimates comparing these two approximations. Finally, we prove that the original interacting queueing system converges exponentially fast to stationarity.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Sarotte, Nahuel Soprano-Loto, Fran\c{c}ois Baccelli

item.title: Asymptotic Behaviour for Isotropic Pearson Random Walks
item.description: arXiv:2609.05195v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the Pearson random walk, the direction of the i-th step is a random variable uniformly distributed on the unit sphere of R^d, and its length is a non-negative random variable. We prove that, when d goes to infinity, the Euclidean norm of the walk converges almost surely to the Euclidean norm of the vector of step lengths, whose joint law is arbitrary. Further, we investigate the same convergence result in a more general framework, where both the number and the lengths of the steps depend on the dimension. The results in the present paper can be applied to approximate the distribution of some classical Pearson random walks, for example, in the Dirichlet case.
item.dc:creator: Davide A. Bignamini, Emanuele G. Casini, Andrea Martinelli

item.title: Sharp propagation of chaos for mean-field backward stochastic differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.15798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quantitative propagation of chaos for mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations with interactions through the empirical measures of the forward states, backward values, and diagonal martingale integrands. Our main contribution is to introduce an intermediate-particle comparison method that transfers forward propagation of chaos estimates to the backward system while controlling the full matrix of martingale integrands. Using this method, we establish sharp rates for the backward values and diagonal martingale integrands, with order $m^2/n^2$ in squared Wasserstein distance and order $n^{-1}$ in smooth weak metrics for each fixed $m$. Explicit examples provide matching lower bounds, showing the optimality of these rates. We also establish coupling estimates, including a squared Wasserstein bound of order $m/n$ with dimension-independent constants under suitable assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Shuxian Gao, Ying Hu, Jiaqiang Wen

item.title: Concentration of bounded sparse chaoses and sparse Khatri--Rao embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2609.28875v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove moment and mixed-tail inequalities for decoupled homogeneous chaoses of arbitrary fixed order generated by independent, centered, bounded random variables with coordinate-dependent second-moment bounds. The estimates hold for arbitrary real rectangular coefficient tensors and are expressed through weighted slice and partition norms. A Bennett-type logarithmic correction sharpens the contribution of the largest coefficient to these bounds. The proof combines a comparison with sums of sparse exponential variables with an elementary replication argument. We also extend the results to diagonal-free non-decoupled chaoses and sparse sub-exponential inputs. As an application, we establish conditions under which sparse Khatri--Rao random projections approximately preserve norms and inner products for finite collections of tensors. For a sparse random relation containing a planted dense block, we prove matching upper and lower bounds on the required projection dimension, demonstrating the sharpness of the logarithmic correction.
item.dc:creator: Guozheng Dai, Yiyun He, Ke Wang, Yizhe Zhu

item.title: Regularity lemma for Gaussian polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.16180v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a regularity lemma for polynomials with fixed degree $d$ and any number of standard Gaussian input variables. Following modern approaches to the Szemer{\'e}di regularity lemma, we deduce our results from a general formulation of the regularity lemma using ultraproducts. Along the way, we give a direct combinatorial proof of the celebrated ``fourth moment theorem'' of Nualart and Peccati, which characterizes the asymptotically Gaussian polynomials inside degree-$d$ Gaussian chaos as those such that $\mathbb{E} p^2 \to 1$ and $\mathbb{E} p^4 \to 3$. We apply the regularity lemma to obtain a short proof of the robust Borell inequality of Mossel and Neeman.
item.dc:creator: Chris Jones

item.title: Phase-Space Realization of Stochastic Multivalued Dynamics with Gyroscopic Subdifferential Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.38381v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new framework for stochastic variational inequalities with oblique reflections generated by non-symmetric matrix coefficients. The loss of symmetry fundamentally changes the structure of the reflected dynamics: besides the dissipative component, it produces a genuinely gyroscopic component describing rotational effects that are invisible to the associated energy forms. To capture this hidden component, we consider planar obstacle problems and we lift the dynamics to an extended phase-space system, where the dissipative and gyroscopic mechanisms are naturally separated. This leads to a new notion of solution, for which we establish existence and uniqueness. The resulting framework allows for genuinely rotated reflections, which can lead to angle-controlled rotations.
item.dc:creator: Ioana Ciotir, Andreea Negrut-Grajdeanu, Eduard Rotenstein

item.title: Tracy-Widom law for sample covariance matrices under quadratic form concentration
item.description: arXiv:2610.41416v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study sample covariance matrices formed from vectors $q_i = \Sigma^{1/2}u_i \in \mathbb{R}^M$, $1 \leq i \leq N$, where $u_1, \ldots, u_N$ are independent, centered, isotropic random vectors whose coordinates may not be independent. We assume that the random vectors $q_i$ satisfy a concentration bound for their quadratic forms $q_i^T A q_i$. Under this assumption and a regular right edge condition on $\Sigma$, we establish edge universality and obtain the Tracy-Widom law for the largest eigenvalue of the sample covariance matrix after appropriate centering and scaling. In particular, for log-concave ensembles, our result removes the unconditionality assumption imposed in existing edge universality results~\cite{BX}, resolving the question that originally motivated our work. The concentration assumption also allows us to extend the result beyond the log-concave class.
item.dc:creator: Guangchen Chen, Xing Lyu

item.title: Gaussian Products: Deterministic Principal Ideals and Wick Order Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2611.03495v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For fixed Hilbert--Schmidt operators $A,B$ and a standard Gaussian array $G$, the algebraic principal ideal generated by $AGB$ almost surely equals a deterministic ideal obtained by multiplying the square tails of $s(A)$ and $s(B)$. In fixed coordinates, the corresponding singular-value comparisons hold simultaneously for all nonincreasing square-summable diagonal weights. We characterize the numerical arrays with this uniform realization property on any two prescribed rank flags by rectangular operator-norm upper bounds and Hilbert--Schmidt lower bounds; the optimal universal upper dilation is two. A family of strictly positive factors reflects every inclusion of principal ideals if and only if its tail-rank profiles have no common eventual upper bound. Otherwise, every local flag region contains a common fibre whose input ideals form a copy of $\mathcal P(\mathbb N)/\mathrm{Fin}$ as a sublattice. For a specified family of operator-valued Gaussian chaoses, Wick composition with one fixed random operator yields principal ideals that recover these inclusion relations. The random ideal identities hold almost surely for each fixed parameter choice.
item.dc:creator: Guangqian Zhao

item.title: Community detection with the Bethe-Hessian
item.description: arXiv:2411.02835v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Bethe-Hessian matrix, introduced by Saade, Krzakala, and Zdeborov\'a (2014), is a Hermitian matrix designed for applying spectral clustering algorithms to sparse networks. Rather than employing a non-symmetric and high-dimensional non-backtracking operator, a spectral method based on the Bethe-Hessian matrix is conjectured to also reach the Kesten-Stigum detection threshold in the sparse stochastic block model (SBM). We provide the first rigorous analysis of the Bethe-Hessian spectral method in the SBM under both the bounded expected degree and the growing degree regimes. Specifically, we demonstrate that: (i) When the expected degree $d\geq 2$, the number of negative outliers of the Bethe-Hessian matrix can consistently estimate the number of blocks above the Kesten-Stigum threshold, thus confirming a conjecture from Saade, Krzakala, and Zdeborov\'a (2014) for $d\geq 2$. (ii) For sufficiently large $d$, its eigenvectors can be used to achieve weak recovery. (iii) As $d\to\infty$, we establish the concentration of the locations of its negative outlier eigenvalues, and weak consistency can be achieved via a spectral method based on the Bethe-Hessian matrix.
item.dc:creator: Ludovic Stephan, Yizhe Zhu

item.title: Stochastic Optimal Control with Measurable Coefficients and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2502.02352v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider fully non-linear stochastic optimal control problems with measurable coefficients and (local) uniformly elliptic diffusion. Using the theory of $L^p$-viscosity solutions, we show existence of an $L^p$-viscosity solution $v\in W_{\rm loc}^{2,p}$ of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, which, in turn, is also a strong solution (i.e. it satisfies the HJB equation pointwise a.e.). We are then led to prove verification theorems, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality. These results allow us to construct optimal feedback controls and to characterize the value function as the unique $L^p$-viscosity solution of the HJB equation. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first results for fully non-linear stochastic optimal control problems with measurable coefficients. We use the theory developed to solve a stochastic optimal control problem arising in economics within the context of optimal advertising.
item.dc:creator: Filippo de Feo

item.title: The superposition principle for the continuity equation with singular flux
item.description:
arXiv:2506.15333v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Representation results for absolutely continuous curves $\mu:[0,T]	o \mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $p>1$, with values in the Wasserstein space $(\mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d),W_p)$ of Borel probability measures in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite $p$-moment, provide a crucial tool to study evolutionary PDEs in a measure-theoretic setting. They are strictly related to the superposition principle for measure-valued solutions to the continuity equation. This paper addresses the extension of these results to the case $p=1$, and to curves $\mu:[0,+\infty)	o\mathcal{P}_1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that are only of bounded variation in time: in the corresponding continuity equation, the flux measure $
u\in\mathcal{M}_{loc}([0,+\infty)	imes\mathbb{R}^{d};\mathbb{R}^{d})$ thus possesses a non-trivial singular part w.r.t. $\mu$ in addition to the absolutely continuous part featuring the velocity field. Firstly, we carefully address the relation between curves in ${m BV}_{loc}([0,+\infty);\mathcal{P}_1(\mathbb{R}^d))$ and solutions to the associated continuity equation, among which we select those with minimal singular (contribution to the) flux $
u$. We show that, with those distinguished solutions it is possible to associate an `auxiliary' continuity equation, in an augmented phase space, solely driven by its velocity field. For that continuity equation, a standard version of the superposition principle can be thus obtained. In this way, we derive a first probabilistic representation of the pair $(\mu,
u)$ solutions by projection over the time and space marginals. This representation involves Lipschitz trajectories in the augmented phase space, reparametrized in time and solving the characteristic system of ODEs. Finally, for the same pair $(\mu,
u)$ we also prove a superposition principle in terms of BV curves on the actual time interval, providing a fine description of their behaviour at jump points.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Almi, Riccarda Rossi, Giuseppe Savar\'e

item.title: Distribution of mixed character sums and extremal problems for Littlewood polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2510.06161v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove distributional results for mixed character sums \begin{equation*}\sum_{n\le x }\chi(n)e(n\theta),\end{equation*} for fixed $\theta\in [0,1]$ and random character $\chi \pmod q$, as well as for a fixed character $\chi$ and randomly sampled $\theta\in [0,1].$ We present various applications of our results. For example, we construct Littlewood polynomials with large Mahler measure and $L_1$ norm, thus establishing new records in the Mahler and Newman problems. We also prove asymptotics for the $L_{2k}$ norms of well-known Turyn polynomials as $k\to\infty$, refuting a conjecture of G\"unther and Schmidt. An important ingredient in our work is a general way of dealing with "log-integrability" problems.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan W. Bober, Oleksiy Klurman, Besfort Shala

item.title: Theoretical guarantees for stochastic gradient sampling methods via Gaussian convolution inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2604.24632v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive first-order (in the stepsize) bounds on the bias in Wasserstein distances of the invariant measure of stochastic gradient kinetic Langevin dynamics with minimal assumptions on the stochastic gradient noise. These bounds sharpen existing non-asymptotic guarantees for stochastic-gradient MCMC methods and provide a quantitative resolution of a previously open problem on invariant measure accuracy. The main technical ingredients are new Gaussian convolution inequalities controlling the Wasserstein-$p$ distance between a Gaussian convolved with a mean-zero perturbation and the Gaussian itself. We anticipate that these inequalities will be of independent interest beyond the present application. To complement the theory, we illustrate the benefits of stochastic gradient sampling methods on a one-dimensional model, a Bayesian logistic regression example and a Bayesian random-effect model including comparison with pseudo-marginal MCMC methods.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Paulin, Peter A. Whalley

item.title: Mean field games with option to buy information
item.description: arXiv:2606.09784v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a class of continuous time finite horizon mean field games where the objective function of the representative player depends on a hidden state, in addition to position, control, and the population distribution. While acting on the position dynamics, the agent has the option to pay for seeing the hidden state. We connect the original formulation of our model with a mean field model of optimal control with discretionary stopping, characterize solutions, and give a simple explicitly solvable example. For a class of $N$-player games with compatible information structure, we show that approximate Nash equilibria can be constructed starting from a solution to the limit model.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo D'Auria, Markus Fischer

item.title: Causal Inference for Sequential Settings under Interference and Latent Confounding
item.description: arXiv:2607.14940v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study causal inference under outcome interference for sequential, observational settings. Specifically, we consider settings where the binary outcomes over N units are Markovian across T time steps. At each time step, the outcomes of N units have dependencies captured through an Ising model; each outcome is also impacted through an external field capturing the effects of its treatment as well as latent confounders. Similar to panel data literature, these latent confounders are modeled to have a low-rank factor structure. Our data is a single sample from this high-dimensional distribution. To estimate causal quantities of interest, we provide a computationally efficient method based on Maximum Pseudo-Likelihood Estimation (MPLE) for learning the model parameters. Under mild assumptions, we establish non-asymptotic consistency for parameter estimation and show this translates to faithful estimation of causal quantities of interest after sampling from the learned model. We demonstrate the efficacy of the method through synthetic experiments as well as a real-world case-study investigating causal effects of vaccine rates on COVID-19 death rates within US counties nationwide.
item.dc:creator: Phevos Paschalidis, Constantinos Daskalakis, Devavrat Shah

item.title: Stochastic Gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews Integrator with Second Order Discretization Error
item.description: arXiv:2610.24781v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) has a discretization error of first order in the step size $h$, even with the full gradient. We study the stochastic gradient Leimkuhler--Matthews (SGLM) integrator, which has the same cost as SGLD, one stochastic gradient per step, and reuses each Gaussian vector in consecutive steps. With the full gradient, SGLM is the Leimkuhler--Matthews (LM) integrator, whose discretization error for the invariant distribution is of second order. For a potential strongly convex outside a ball, we prove the bound $\mathcal O(\frac{1}{Nh} + \Sigma^2 h^2 + h^4)$ on the mean square error (MSE) of time averages of SGLM over $N$ steps, where $\Sigma$ bounds the variance of the gradient noise. The proof uses a modified class that absorbs the non-Markovian part of SGLM. The discretization error enters this bound as $h^4$ and the MSE bound of SGLD as $h^2$, while a larger batch reduces only the term $\Sigma^2 h^2$ in both bounds. In Bayesian logistic regression on MNIST, SGLM has a smaller estimated MSE than SGLD. The coefficient of $h$ in the numerical bias of SGLM is given explicitly by the covariance of the gradient noise and the continuous Poisson equation. The coefficient for SGLD contains in addition the Hessian of the potential, which comes from the discretization error. Through Riesz representors, the coefficients of the numerical bias determine the coefficients of the Wasserstein-1 errors of SGLM and SGLD.
item.dc:creator: Xuda Ye, Yuliang Wang, Guang Lin, Cindy Xiangrui Kong
